query: What signals suggest a travel expense will be declined?

per_column.name: missing_source_id
per_column.rationale: A missing source_id flag is derivable directly from the source_id column and plausibly correlates with data-entry anomalies relevant to declines. Moderately useful as a new axis, well grounded.

per_column.name: no_processed_date
per_column.rationale: Directly derived from processed_date (nan handled correctly, as seen in the sample). A missing processed date is a plausible signal for unprocessed/declined items; grounded and reasonably useful.

per_column.name: amount_above_travel_median
per_column.rationale: Compares amount against the travel-category median, giving a genuine new axis directly relevant to whether a travel expense is atypical/declined. Derivable from amount and category.

per_column.name: amount_below_dept_median
per_column.rationale: Relative amount within department; a distinct comparative axis from the travel-median flag. Grounded in amount and department.

per_column.name: user_prior_decline_rate
per_column.rationale: Per-user historical decline rate is a strong, high-variance predictor directly aligned with the query. Derivable from user and state across rows, though it presumes prior-history ordering; values look reasonable.

per_column.name: high_decline_dept
per_column.rationale: Flags departments with elevated decline rates, a useful grouping axis. Derivable from department and state aggregation; somewhat correlated with user rate but distinct at dept level.

per_column.name: submitted_off_hours
per_column.rationale: Off-hours flag derived from a timestamp (likely opened_at/processed_date). Plausibly weak signal for declines; grounded but its usefulness for THIS query is moderate and near-even distribution limits leverage.

per_column.name: decline_risk_score
per_column.rationale: A composite score aggregating the other flags provides a convenient ranking axis, but it is largely a restatement/combination of already-added columns and its weighting is opaque; samples show it can be 0 even when component flags are set, raising derivation questions.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine, distinct analytical axes for predicting travel-expense declines (user/department decline rates, relative-amount comparisons, missingness flags) and are soundly derivable from table fields; the missing/processed-date handling in the samples is correct. Weaknesses: submitted_off_hours is a fairly generic timestamp-derived flag with modest leverage, and decline_risk_score is largely a composite restatement of the other flags with an opaque, sometimes inconsistent derivation. Overall the set is useful and well grounded on the two necessary conditions.
